column1: # analysis/naming/ram_g3.tsv - RAM name proposals derived from banks 2A/2B/2C (config/ram format; the orchestrator reconciles against config/ram)

# NOTE: every address below was also proposed independently by other passes (ram_g2.tsv: C2EE; ram_g4.tsv: the rest); the names are deliberately IDENTICAL to theirs, so the rows only add corroborating evidence from banks 2A/2B/2C (safe to merge as duplicates)

column6: replaces wRam_C2EE: remaining six-pixel cells of the draw-string routines; set to the field width ($10/$14/$15/$19..) on entry (2A:4483, 2A:5952, 2B:4421, 2B:7DF2, 2C:431D, 2C:614D), -1 per half-width glyph, -2 per 2-byte glyph; loop ends at 0, the tail loop pads blanks while >0

replaces wRam_C2AD: low (trail) byte of the Shift-JIS char chosen on the bank-55 keyboard; compared with $4A/$4B (marks 814A/814B = dakuten/handakuten) at 2A:61DC/61FA and 2C:499B/49B8, loaded into E and inserted after D (2A:620E, 2C:49CB); zeroed by Profile_ApplyDakuten on success (2A:5F36)
replaces wRam_C2AE: high (lead) byte of the Shift-JIS char chosen on the bank-55 keyboard; compared with $81 (2A:61E3, 2A:6201, 2C:49A2, 2C:49BF) and loaded into D before insertion (2A:6212, 2C:49CF)

replaces wRam_C0D2: text-cursor column mirrored after every horizontal move (2A:5767/57AF, 2C:40F7/413D/4148 ...) and read back by the vertical-move code of bank 2D (loads at 2D:495F, 2D:498A: c=min([C0D2], line length))

replaces wRam_C0D3: SCY applied below the split line by the STAT handler 00:0E93 (ld a,[C0D3]; ldh [rSCY],a); subtracted from the y of the text-cursor sprites (2A:5920, 2C:4300); set to $24 when the title keyboard opens (2C:4245), 0 on exit (2C:49F6, 2A:5718)

replaces wRam_D400 (WRAM bank1): $C0-byte mail body edit buffer, staged with SRAM $A040 by 2D:403C/408F; 2B:7B9B copies received record+9 ($C0 B) here and draws it as 8 lines of 24 cells (2B:7EE0/7DF2)

replaces wRam_D4C0 (WRAM bank1): $40-byte mail address / e-mail buffer, staged with SRAM $A000 by 2D:403C/408F; profile address loaded from $AF50 (2A:6257); address-book slot+$10 copied in (2C:57F1) and out (2A:704B); drawn as 20/24/20 chars (2B:420C)

replaces wRam_D500 (WRAM bank1): $14-byte mail title/subject buffer (10 double-byte kana), staged with SRAM $A100 by 2D:403C/408F; edited by MailTitle_* (2C:44B8, 4612, 4A05 limit $14); drawn at y=$14 by 2B:420C

replaces wRam_D514 (WRAM bank1): $10-byte name buffer (8 double-byte chars), staged with SRAM $A114 by 2D:403C/408F; profile nickname loaded from/saved to $AF40 (2A:6257/62C5), edited by Profile_* (2A:5CD2 tests the last cell D522); address-book slot+0 copied in/out (2C:57F1, 2A:704B)

replaces wRam_D524: compose mode 1 new (2D:4011 in the compose entry 2D:4000), 2 edit written mail (2B:4743 writes 2), 3 reply (25:5515 in Mailbox_ReplyToRecord 25:54A7; dead twin write at 2B:6D5D); CAVEAT: 2B:691A (MailView_DrawDateTime) uses D524..D52F as digit scratch while a received mail is shown, so the byte is only a mode inside the compose flow
